articleTitle: Multi-motor solutions for electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: For classic vehicles powered by internal combustion engines, the gearbox and the mechanical transmission with differential system sustain the obtention of needed torque at wheels. Combining different gears, the vehicle attempts a large speed range. However, the use of electric propulsion systems that produce high torque at zero speed suppresses or limits the usage of the gearbox to one reducer in the most cases. Also, bringing the mechanical power generation from a central point for all the car to the wheels by modular design, becomes an opportunity with electric motors. This paper presents the multi-electric engine solution for a vehicle passing from one motor solution (all wheels driving) to two motors design. The comparative analysis of the dynamic and electrical parameters of the two solutions was performed using numerical simulation. The obtained results showed that the solution with two engines has certain advantages, at least in terms of energy consumption.

articleTitle: Smart Grid Communication and Networking: Review of Standards
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Smart grid gives a new and improved vision for electricity infrastructure. The vital element of the smart grid is the bidirectional communication between the grid and its users. Hence, communication plays a basic role in establishing the connectivity between various constituents of the smart grid. One must have a detailed understanding of various aspects of communication to establish robust network connectivity. Integration of network components from various vendors may not follow the same set of canons, thereby, it becomes difficult to establish a network that can be accepted globally. Thus, before deploying a network in real-time, it is always recommended to test the model using simulation tools, where, various standards can be tested by changing key parameters. Once the optimum solution is achieved in the simulation, it can be deployed using the hardware components. With this intent, this paper provides a systematic review of the key IEC and IEEE standards related to smart grid communication and networking.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Rotor Field-Orientation Control for Induction Traction Motor
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the synthesis of rotor field-orientation control for an induction motor intended for the electric traction of an autonomous locomotive powered by a battery. The operating equations in the system with rotor field-orientation and the associated control scheme are presented and discussed. After presenting the structural scheme and the operational equations, the design of controllers is addressed. The performance of the control system during the start-up by prescribing a ramp speed and step rotor flux, for two speeds is presented and analyzed. The results validate the correct synthesis of the control system and control algorithm.

articleTitle: Studies Related to the Optimization of an Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine Designed for the Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a study related to the optimization of a 150 kW interior permanent magnet synchronous machine with rotor magnets in delta configuration used for an electric vehicle. The first part highlights the characteristics of the reference motor. Two mono-objective optimizations studies concerning the minimization of the cogging torque and the minimization of the ripple torque were performed. The performances of the ideal optimized machine and of the unoptimized machine are compared using Altair HyperStudy and FluxMotor software packages, which combine analytical calculation with finite element analysis and also using the genetic algorithm method.

articleTitle: Maximum Power Point Tracking – A Study of Photovoltaic Systems in Supplying Stand-Alone and Grid-Connected Electrical Loads
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper proposes two appropriate control methods for Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) of a photovoltaic system in stand-alone and grid-connected conditions. Two algorithms were applied in this article: Incremental Conductance and Innovative Fuzzy Control. These algorithms were simulated and compared; therefore, on the basis of the best algorithm, the influence of environmental factors such as temperature and radiation intensity on the photovoltaic array and the controllers' response were studied. The control strategy in grid-connected condition was based on Instantaneous Reactive Power theory and inverter switching was implemented using the Adaptive Hysteresis method. The MATLAB simulation results illustrated the acceptable performance of the proposed system in achieving MPPT for two conditions of stand-alone and grid-connected loads due to the variable temperature and radiation. Furthermore, results indicated the compensation of current harmonics and reactive power of nonlinear loads.

articleTitle: Design of improved mechatronic system for Virtusphere
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Following a previous study on VirtuSphere (VS) platform improvement solutions, it was concluded that a mechatronic system integrated with the platform could offer the possibility of immersion. The purpose of the mechatronic system is to provide feedback to the user using brushless motors. During the development of the mechatronic system, the authors noticed its limited capacity and certain possibilities to improve the initial design. This article presents the concept of an improved version of the system integrated with the VS platform by using omnidirectional wheels. The characteristics of the mechanical components were determined by calculation. Based on this information the authors designed the components of the system as well as the omnidirectional wheels with features compatible to application because they are not available on the market.

articleTitle: Efficient Real-Time Object Detection based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Visual objects recognition based on deep learning with the CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) have been extensive developments in computer image algorithms and improvements in computer hardware. In this work, a simplified CNN structure with a simple hardware system based on the Raspberry Pi with a compatible camera is developed. It can take pictures or videos in real time to recognize the existence of a human among ten predefined classes. The proposed model is implemented with less memory and less processing power while handling large amounts of data with Pascal VOC and Microsoft COCO datasets. The detection algorithm can quickly distinguish the object in 0.82 seconds and higher. The accuracy reaches 98%.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of HBC Fuses with Aluminium Fuse Element at Minimum Rated Breaking Current
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This article describes an experimental study of high breaking capacity fuses with aluminum fuse element with and without eutectic point at minimum rated breaking current preceded by experiments at maximum rated breaking current. It is shown that, in this construction with aluminum fusible element, the fuse has no problem to break the maximum rated breaking current, it has real difficulties with minimum rated breaking current. The experiments were made on a homogeneous series 6-20 A, with focus on the 36 kV, 25 kA, 16 A fuse, which suffered multiple construction changes and tests with and without eutectic point. It was found an acceptable constructive solution, that passed the tests but the obtained value for the minimum rated breaking current is not a commercial attractive value.

articleTitle: Mathematical modeling and simulation of PV systems Part I: Mathematical modeling and Simulink implementation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In this paper the mathematical modeling and Simulink implementation of PV systems is proposed to better understand the characteristics of PV systems whose characteristics are nonlinear. Based on the mathematical modeling, the Simulink implementation is made. The resulting model uses a friendly interface considering the Function Block Parameters to set the parameters of the PV model. The simulation interface helps the user to estimate the power generated by the PV array under different environmental conditions. The interface for the resulting model is easy to use, because the interface allows also the modification of the module parameters, including the ideality factor for polycrystalline (A=1.3) and monocrystalline (A=1.2) photovoltaic cells. The simulation results are shown in part two of the paper. The simulation of PV systems under different atmospheric conditions is performed.

articleTitle: Influence of Experimental Measurements Accuracy on Connector Resistance Factor for Crimped Connections
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In the process of validation of crimped connections, the determination of the connector resistance factor has a decisive role. In this paper is studied the influence of the experimental measurements accuracy on the calculation of this factor, cumulating data from various types of crimped connections. The measurements were performed on barrel of terminal lug type for three cross sections of cables. The relative initial scatter of the mean of the connector resistance factors is influenced by 6 representative measured quantities as voltage drops, currents and conductor lengths. First, the maximum allowed variation of each quantity was calculated, the others being kept constant, having as effect the variation by one unit of hundredths digit of initial scatter, then simultaneous variations of the 6 quantities caused by device reading errors were imposed, determining the quantities with the greatest influence. Useful recommendations for experimenter are made.

articleTitle: Teaching and Research in Emerging Electrical Energy Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents emerging engineering educational issues in topics of electric energy, linked to the specialized knowledge of graduates, and to the institutions asking specific positions. Interdisciplinary subtopics of energy engineering education are renewable energy generation, electrical motion systems, dedicated computers software and hardware, internet of things, management and economics. European initiatives were undertaking the design and development of electric energy programs of study, to become more oriented to the requirements of industry. The impact of electric energy industry in the programs of studies will influence the competencies of graduates, and offer new jobs for them, that diminishes the unemployment and migration abroad of talented professionals. The important matters are the educating of young engineers in specialties essential for their professional work. The laboratory and experimental part of programs of studies must be boosted to prepare better the future engineers.

articleTitle: Solar Tracking System for Several Groups of Solar Panels
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Solar tracking systems have proven their effectiveness and thereby justified their cost price. They orient solar panels and increase the conversion of solar energy into electricity. Positioning systems work based on different methods and principles. In most cases they are individual systems attached to a single solar panel array. This paper presents a proposal for a system to control the solar orientation of a virtually unlimited group of solar panels located in the same geographical area. It allows orientation along two axes, with reduced costs due to the own consumption of the orientation motors.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Efficiency of a Stand-Alone PV System for Powering of a Detached House in the Village of Nikolovo, Bulgaria
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In the present study the possibilities for application of stand-alone PV systems for powering of detached houses located in agricultural areas are analyzed. The environmental conditions of a village near Ruse, Bulgaria and a typical seasonal load profiles are considered. The PV system is sized using the PVsyst 7.1 software for 45° tilt angle, southern orientation and 2 days of autonomy. The average unused energy varies from 0.5 to 3 kWh/kWp/day, which corresponds to 33% of the produced PV energy. The study also analyzes the possibilities for utilizing the excess energy in processes with variable load profile. Considering the geographic location of the house, the possible applications include pumping of irrigation water, climatization of greenhouses, outdoor lighting, etc.

articleTitle: The Choice of the IGBTs and their Cooling in Electric Traction Converters for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: An important stage for the electric traction converters design is the choice of the power components and their cooling system. This paper is focused on the choice of the IGBT modules, their cooling and over-temperature protection in a test bench for electric traction converters designed for autonomous vehicles. Various possible applications on battery-powered vehicles together with their technical, functional characteristics and performances were taken into account in defining the parameters of the test bench, an important share belonging to the integrated Li-Ion battery propulsion/charging system developed by INDA. It is already used in the railway field on electric locomotives with batteries and in automotive on full electric trucks.

articleTitle: Smart Storage and Grid Services Based on Removable Modular Batteries for EV
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The wider use of renewable sources and of electric vehicles has to be supported by smart storage. Becoming modular and removable, battery charging and use differ temporally and spatially. This increases both the EV and the grid flexibility, makes it easier to purchase EVs, avoid useless reinforcement of the grid and postpone investment until recurring congestions occur. The EV owners can rent charged batteries for on board or domestic use. Aggregators can deploy removable batteries or include them in virtual power plants, virtual power lines, utility scale batteries in order to provide smart grid services, capacity firming of variable renewable sources. Better usability, care and recycling are achieved when battery management is done by professionals. All these concepts are first explained and then illustrated by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Efficient Topology of Powering a Washing Machine Using a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The need to wash clothes is a task performed in households since the existence of modern humanity. In the last century the development of home appliances has led to washing machines being present in each home. As the number of devices is increasing, the need for efficient products is becoming more and more important. This paper presents an energy efficient topology of powering a washing machine, with the field oriented control (FOC) of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). The washing machine needs a low speed-high torque to wash the laundry and a high speed with a lower torque to spin it until dry. These two different specification requirements can be achieved by driving the motor with MTPA (Maximum Torque Per Ampere) and Field Weakening (FW ) strategies.

articleTitle: Isotropic near field measurement system for new generation communication signals: Preliminary design and USRP calibration
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In the present article we propose a solution based on Software Defined Radio for isotropic, real-time, and simultaneous measurement of six channels corresponding to six field probes (electric and magnetic). The measurement system is much needed for exposure evaluation campaigns conducted in the near field of emitting devices (mobile phone, WLAN router, etc.). However, the use of an SDR pose other problems that need careful and precise solving, to report accurate field levels. To this extent, in this work we present the calibration of an instrument model USRP N310 in the n78 5G (3.5-3.7 GHz) frequency band. The instrument response is investigated for a 5G-like signal, namely a 20 MHz wide, LTE-A, OFDM signal. The instrument sensitivity is analysed in function of the used channel bandwidth and compared to a mid-range swept spectrum analyser sensitivity. The frequency and amplitude response of the instrument are commented on. Results suggest suitability of the instrument for the proposed measurement system. To increase the accuracy of the measured field levels a quick frequency response calibration is indicated before each measurement campaign.

articleTitle: Real-Time Sensorless Control of PMSM and SCADA Integration
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This article presents an application of real-time control of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) and its integration into Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition (SCADA). Starting from the operating equations of the PMSM and by implementing the global Field Oriented Control (FOC) control strategy, in which the saturation of the integral component of the PI-type controller is prevented by using an anti-windup technique, the numerical simulations performed in Matlab/Simulink lead to good performance, which recommends the real-time implementation. The numerical simulation step is necessary to choose the type of Digital Signal Processing (DSP) used for the real-time implementation, considering that a global criterion of successful implementation is the performance/cost ratio. Moreover, the integration into SCADA provides flexibility of the control system but also the possibility of online/offline processing from the point of view of other specific requirements. Among them we mention the energy quality analysis, whose first exponent calculated also in real-time is Total Harmonic Distortion (THD). Real-time implementations are performed in Matlab/Simulink and LabVIEW programming environments. According to the trend of the last years, the use of an Internet of Things (IoT) platform for viewing the variables of the control process on the Internet has a special place.

articleTitle: Measurements of Shielding Effectiveness at a Faraday Flexible Enclosure
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: To reduce electromagnetic disturbances and to ensure protection against electromagnetic interference, current research aims to produce lightweight and low cost absorbent materials. In this sense, companies are looking for innovative, environmentally friendly and economical solutions for the production of high quality products for protection against electromagnetic interferences. As a result, Faraday flexible enclosures made of highly conductive textiles made of polyester with cooper and nickel were manufactured. These enclosures are used for electromagnetic compatibility experiments as well for protection of people. This paper presents some measurements made considering IEEE Std. 299, performed for the evaluation of shielding effectiveness on a Faraday flexible enclosure. The measurements are performed in a special laboratory from a Romanian Institute for Research, Development and Testing in Electrical Engineering.

articleTitle: Improved Control Strategy of Unified Power Quality Conditioner Using Fractional Order Controller and Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: It is well known that the role of the Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC) is to improve power quality on both the source side and on the load side. In this article, to improve the performance of the UPQC, the classic Proportional Integrator (PI) controller is replaced with a Fractional Order PI (FO-PI) controller, in which the order of the integrator is fractional, thus providing an additional degree of freedom. The most important elements of the UPQC are a series active power filter, respectively a parallel active power filter. The tuning of the parameters of the controllers of these active power filters is performed using a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) method. The main element of comparison consists in maintaining the steady voltage in the DC intermediate circuit. The superior performance of the FO-PI controller is validated by numerical simulations performed in the Matlab/Simulink development environment.

articleTitle: Virtual Instrumentation for Power Quality Analysis in the Main Supplying Point at Entrance of an Industrial Consumer
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present a practical system based on virtual instrumentation for analysis of industrial consumer power quality. This analyzer is implemented using hardware components (voltage and current transducers for instantaneous values; USB data acquisition module; laptop) and software (LabVIEW graphical programming environment). The acquisition of three currents and three voltages allows the proposed system to calculate on line and off line several parameters that characterize the electric power quality. The waveforms of currents and voltages can be viewed individually or all at once. Also, can computes and analyze: the average of Fast Fourier Transform FFT spectrum of time signals, the value of the total harmonic distortion factor THD, the fundamental frequency, the components level with the rms values of the measured harmonics. The total powers (active, reactive, apparent) and by components values are calculated; total three-phase power factor is also calculated. The proposed system allows data acquisition and implicitly power quality monitoring in a user-defined time interval. The system was tested in the secondary of the power transformer of an industrial consumer in the field of repair and maintenance of railway equipment. The validation of the obtained results was done by direct comparison with the indications of a Fluke 435 three-phase power quality analyzer.

articleTitle: Investigation of Electric Load Profiles in Industrial Poultry Farms
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The study presents experimental results from an investigation of the group load profiles in an industrial poultry farm. The results were obtained using an energy monitoring system for a 6 months period – from July to December 2019. The experimental data, which was collected with a step of one hour, was then statistically analyzed on a monthly basis in order to obtain the hourly average load as well as its 95% confidence interval. Furthermore, several group coefficients of the active power were obtained aimed at providing in-depth information about the electrical regimes in the farm. For this are used the shape factor, the utilization factor, and the output factor. Additionally, the ordered load profiles were obtained for each of the investigated months. Then the results were compared with the information regarding the technological processes in the farm in order to assess the dependencies. Conclusions were made regarding the optimal structure of power generators based on solar energy.

articleTitle: Mathematical modeling and simulation of PV systems Part II: Simulation results
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In the first part of the paper the mathematical modeling and Simulink implementation of PV systems is made. The friendly interface resulting after the simulation is similar with block libraries of the Simulink program. By using this model, the PV characteristics under different levels of irradiation, temperature, Partial Shading Conditions (PSC) can be determined easily. The second part of the paper presents the simulation results for PV systems under different atmospheric conditions. Thus, the PV characteristics under different values of irradiation (250 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 500 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 750 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 1000 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and constant temperature (25°C), under different values of temperature ( 0°C, 25°C, 40°C, 65°C) and constant irradiation (1000W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), and the PV characteristics under PSC are also presented .

articleTitle: Setting Digital Relay Protection in Wind Farms Using Similitude Criteria Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper studies the protection equipment of wind farms connected to the transmission or to the distribution network. The main goal is to study a wind farm equipped with static shunt compensator and STATCOM, integrated in a medium voltage network. The solution of the wind generator which uses squirrel cage induction generators has the advantage of low investment and maintenance costs. However, specific to induction machines is the high absorption of reactive power, in this case obviously, from the network. On the experimental laboratory model, the short-circuit currents are determined by the method of per units, depending on the reactance of the equipment in the transformer substation and the line, up to the point of common coupling. The methodology for setting or checking the adjustments of the protection relays is established, on an experimental laboratory model. The experimental determinations, for medium voltage faults on the lines radially connected to the main the line emerging from the wind farm, using the similarity relations, permit the determination of the electrical quantities from the real network. The modeling is performed on a laboratory network that allows the simulation of the faults in the lines, depending on the adjustments of the protection system. Finally, a comparison is made between the values designed for the real network and those resulting from the modeling on the network implemented in the laboratory.

articleTitle: An Overview of Acceleration Detection in Inertial Navigation Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Accelerometers, along with gyros are the basis of inertial navigation systems, these being the main components of the inertial detection unit. This paper presents an overview of the main categories of accelerometers currently available, as well as a market statistic for this segment. It is also presented a current situation in a pandemic context, and how much this inconvenience could influence the future market. The three types of accelerometers reviewed here, are presented at the level of operating principles and general equations.

articleTitle: Inertial Measurement Unit – A Short Overview of the Evolving Trend for Miniaturization and Hardware Structures
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Inertial navigation is an important concern nowadays, being divided into gimbaled gyro-stabilized platforms and strap-down systems. Between the two systems, the most used, especially in the aerospace field, is the strap- down systems, involving accelerometers and gyro sensors, these being the main component of the inertial measurement unit. This paper presents an overview of the currently inertial navigation systems (INS) structures as well as the hardware configuration of the inertial measurement units (IMU), highlighting the miniaturized MEMS technology.

articleTitle: Considerations on the Harmonic Regime Produced by the Faults Appeared in the Medium Voltage Networks with the Neutral Treated by Extinguishing Coil
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The authors present in this paper the results they obtained after the extension of their research and in the field of harmonic regime produced by the grounding of a power line. This type of fault occurs frequently in the case of medium voltage networks, with neutral treated with extinguishing coil. Thus, they managed to reconstruct the waveforms of currents and voltages during the fault period (grounding). Then, having these calculation elements available, a comparative analysis of similar incidents (earthing) from a 20 kV network with the neutral treated with classic extinguishing coil and modern Trench extinguishing coil, respectively, was made.

articleTitle: Small Scale Model of Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The air quality from closed spaces is very important for people or for technological processes. The heating, ventilation and air conditioning installations ensure the maintenance of the air parameters in the rooms served within pre-established limits, throughout the year, regardless of the variation of meteorological factors, the degree of occupancy of the rooms or the development of production processes.The paper presents an automatic ventilation, heating and air conditioning system made on a small scale. The control of the installation is done with a Mega 2560 development system made around the Atmega 2560 microcontroller, which processes the information received from the DHT22 temperature and humidity sensor. The system can be used both for educational purposes for engineering students, but can be adapted for real practical applications.

articleTitle: A New Approach to Speed and Rotor Flux Estimation of Induction Motors for Vector Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach in speed and rotor flux estimation for induction motors. In this sense, the rotor flux is estimated with the help of a new full-order state observer, and the speed is estimated with the help of a back-emf MRAS observer. For the proposed observer its dynamic performances and stability are analyzed. The paper also presents the value range of the proportionality coefficient in the component of the observer gain matrix. The validity of the observer are proved by numerical simulation in Matlab-Simulink.

articleTitle: Improved Performance of a Converter Operating as a Power Interface in Hybrid Microgrids Using Fractional Order PI Controller
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The problem of maintaining a constant DC voltage in a slave microgrid connected by means of an interleaved three-phase converter to a master grid is of a well-known importance. Thus, starting from the detailed description of the topology and mathematical model of the converter operating as a power interface in hybrid microgrids, their transfer functions and the current and voltage controllers in this topology, this article shows that, by using a Fractional Order Proportional Integrator (FO-PI) controller the results obtained are superior as compared to the use of PI classic controllers. The tuning of the FO-PI controller is achieved by using the Fractional-order Modeling and Control (FOMCON) toolbox. The superiority of these controllers, both when there is a disturbance caused by the current flowing through the slave microgrid, and when there is no disturbance is demonstrated by numerical simulations performed in the Matlab/Simulink development environment.

articleTitle: Collaborative Application Between Robots for Industrial Environments
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In some conditions, such as dangerous environments or unfortunate accidents where a human cannot reach the workspace where the robot operates, the solution is to use the feature that collaborative robots can work together whit cooperative robots. In this experiment, a Rethink Robotics Sawyer robot will collaborate with a Kuka youBot, to work together in a workspace where a human operator will not be necessary anymore. Here, the fact that Kuka youBot is a mobile robot is essential. The Sawyer robot can be supplied with materials and can also have the tool changed by the Kuka robot.

articleTitle: Addressing SmartGrid using a practical, scalable and cost-effective home automation solution
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The main objective of the project was to design and make a model based on the concept of "Smart Building", a model called H.A.R.I (HOME AUTOMATION RECHARGED INDEPENDENTLY). The motivation of the project was to find plug-and-play solutions for automation and renewable energy sources that can be easily integrated into any type of home and may be accessed from anywhere, anytime, by any type of user.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of a Free Rare-Earth PMaSynRM for Light Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In the paper is presented a numerical analysis of a free rare-earth permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance machine (PMaSynRM). It will be analyzed a geometrical configuration with six poles on the rotor, whose permanent magnets are made of SrO6Fe2O3. Usually, electric vehicles need reliable and resilient electric motors and today it is a worldwide trend that consists of rare-earth free electrical machines. The efficiency and torque density have to be investigated and optimized, so as a consequence the entire cost of the motor could be reduced. PMaSynRM machine is designed using finite element method (FEM) simulation. The proposed configuration presented in the paper, is analyzed, by taking into account the generator working conditions, as a first step in the new machine configuration design. The cogging torque is computed, using FEM simulations and the three phased electrical voltages are presented.

articleTitle: RSM enhanced ACOR algorithm for electromagnetic optimization
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper studies and proposes the use of RSM (Response Surface Methodology) to enhance the performances of the ACO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</sub> (Ant Colony Optimization for Real domains) algorithm. Several RSM models, such as CCD (Central Composite Design), Box-Behnken and Doelhert, are employed and applied to construct a metaheuristic function in order to find the optimal set of parameters for an ACO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</sub> algorithm when solving an electromagnetic problem. The problem used for testing is a benchmark proposed by the electromagnetic community namely the Loney's solenoid. The ACO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</sub> optimal parameters are searched for two different objectives, the best solution and the average best solution over a set of tests.

articleTitle: Educational Platform for an Underground Smart Parking using Programmable Logic Controllers
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper describes a smart parking system using the Ladder Diagram programming language that can be used by students to understand the principles of a process automation. It is an educational platform that gives information about what elements are part of such programs, how to implement them using a programmable logic controller, how to create a Logical Diagram / Organization Chart and simulate the program. This type of application approach fits well due to the reorganization of the educational teaching system that has been a great challenge for many teachers during the pandemic, not only regarding the teaching curriculum, but also regarding teaching methods. Also, because of the constantly growing digitalization, virtual laboratories and electronic learning platforms must become frequent teaching methods, especially in higher education systems.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis of Multiphase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors with the Same Stators of Analogue 3-phase, 5-phase, 7-phase and 9-phase Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Based on finite element models the performances of four permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) with 3-phase, 5-phase, 7-phase and 9-phase stator winding are evaluated in order to compare these PMS motors with the analogues induction motors and to select the better variant related the number of phases. The influence of the PMSM's rotor fault that consists in the decrease of the remnant magnetic flux density of one of the four magnets on the electromagnetic torque and on the rotor unbalanced force is studied.

Author Keywords: Finite element in time domain analyses

articleTitle: A Truthful Mechanism for Rentals of Privately Owned Electrical Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents an auction of our proposed car renting system for private car owners. While related work relies on the initial renter to return the automobile, our approach to remote opening and starting cars enables them to return to the owner by paying drivers to park them incrementally closer to the owner's preferred drop-off location. Funding for this is provided by the initial renter who abandoned the car in an undesired location. Our mathematical model is designed to increase costs for renters that do not seem to be returning the automobile. We present a fair and truthful way to establish the current cost or renting a car within the system using the algorithmic mechanism of double auctions and we show how this mechanism is truthful and guarantees coverage of maintenance costs of the automobiles.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer Systems: Thévenin Equivalent Circuits for Parallel-Series and Parallel-Parallel Magnetic Resonator Configurations
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents equivalent Thévenin circuits for two connections (parallel-series (ps) and parallel-parallel (pp)), for the magnetic coupling coils (resonators), used in wireless active power transfer. Using the Circuit Symbolic Analysis Program, the equivalent voltage generator in respect of the load terminals in full symbolic form is obtained. It could be seen that all the parameters of the Thévenin generator depend on all the circuit parameters and on the frequency. Based on the maximum active power transfer theorem, the optimal load parameters (connected to the terminals of the receiver coil) are obtained.

articleTitle: Study of Overvoltages at the Extinguishing Coil Disconnection from Medium Voltage Networks in Stabilized Earthing Regime
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Considering that in medium voltage networks with neutral treated by the extinguishing coil there are real difficulties of selective triggering of the line with single-phase defect, the paper presents a study of overvoltages that occur at single-phase faults in medium voltage networks with neutral treated with extinguishing coil, followed by the triggering of the extinguishing coil immediately after the stabilization of the grounding regime. The study is performed by simulating in the Simulink computer program a medium voltage network fed radially from a 110/20 kV transformer station. If the results of the study lead to the conclusion that overvoltages are not dangerous for installations, then for permanent grounding the deliberate disconnection of the extinguishing coil, and thus the transformation of the net neutral treatment from the neutral treated by the extinguishing beret into isolated neutral, will ensure selective triggering of the defective line.

articleTitle: Experimental Determinations of the Influence of Environmental Factors on the Electrical Properties of Some Composite Materials
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Composite materials, which are state-of-the-art materials with special properties, have been used in recent decades in various fields of activity from robotics to medicine, from architectural constructions to sports equipment, from electronics, electrical and IT to aerospace or automotive constructions. That is why it is necessary to carefully study these materials and how environmental factors (heat, cold, humidity etc.) can affect the properties of these materials. This paper was proposed for the experimental determination of the influence of ambient temperature on the value of dielectric strength for some polymeric composite electrical insulating materials. A more special test was also carried out, to which polymeric composite materials are not currently subjected, but which is important for industrial applications in the field of electrical engineering, namely the proof tracking index of solid insulating materials (PTI). The thermal conditioning, the experimental determination of dielectric strength for each material and the verification of the proof tracking index of solid insulating materials were performed in the RENAR accredited laboratory within the National Research, Development and Testing Institute for Electrical Engineering- ICMET Craiova. The experimental results showed that in the case of the studied composite materials, no influences of environmental factors were observed on the dielectric strength values.

articleTitle: Improving the Efficiency of Joint SWT/WPT Analysis by Using Different Wavelet Mothers
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Previous studies related to joint analysis by using Discrete Wavelet Transform and Wavelet Packet transform relying on Daubechies filters of length 28 were considered as a starting point for this paper. Sensibilities to harmonic pollution of levels from Stationary Wavelet Trees relying on Daubechies filters of 28 components, of 40 components and respectively of a truncated version of the last ones (containing only 30 components) were determined and compared. Their performances were evaluated in order to be used in another type of joint analysis, involving Wavelet Packet trees. The same filters were examined afterward relative to the most significant harmonic energies weights in the terminal nodes of a wavelet packet tree with 7 levels used to decompose signals with 512 components per period. Runtimes were evaluated for all types of wavelet transforms (Discrete, Stationary and Packet) and recommendations relative to "best usability" scenarios were issued based on the performed analysis.

articleTitle: The Power Quality Indices influence on the Economics and the Energy Efficiency of industrial end-users
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: As proven by previous works [1] - [3], [7], Power Quality is strongly linked to the global Energy Performance and, implicitly, to the overall Economic Efficiency of any given energy boundary. In this paper, authors will analyse, and present results obtained by implementing a Current Total Harmonic Distortion mitigation solution in an atypical sub-energy boundary belonging to an industrial end-user. The forecasted Technic and Economic viability will be analysed and presented, showing that improving Power Quality Indices leads to an optimization of the Energy Performance Indicators and, ultimately, to a sensible improvement of the Economic Efficiency of the process.

articleTitle: Numerical Study Concerning Longitudinal Dynamic of a Canard UAV with Vectored Thrust
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This work presents a study concerning the possibilities to improve the longitudinal dynamic of a canard UAV using vectored thrust. It is followed to harness the advantages of canard configuration of UAV and to obtain further a better longitudinal dynamic, able to fulfil more complex missions than canard UAV without vectored thrust.

articleTitle: Validation Steps For Vector Control Modelling
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This article presents the validation steps used in vector control of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) with application in home appliances. These steps help assuring that the motor, the transforms used, and the control loop is modeled correctly. The methods presented in the first part of this work refers to vector control with position and speed of the rotor obtained from the motor equations and, in the last part, a position and speed estimation method is implemented and verified. The main advantages of these validation steps are in the clarity of the model development and help to avoid possible hidden errors in a seemingly correct operation.

articleTitle: Robust Observer Based Control Scheme for DC-DC Boost Converter Using LMI
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The linear quadratic regulator with integral action (LQI) method is used in this paper to control DC-DC boost converter. The LQI controller around the operating point of the system can provide the system stability. However, when the control system is in the presence of severe uncertainty, the performance of the LQI controller decreases. So, for the purpose of implementation of the LQI controller in the presence of severe uncertainty, the linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) are employed to enhance the performance of the controller so as to facilitate control action, the proposed scheme needs the information of the both state of the converter including, output voltage and inductor current. However, achieving the exact information of the inductor current in the presence of the noise and uncertainty can lead to deteriorate the control scheme. In this regards, Unscented Kalman filter (UKF) observer is employed to estimate the inductor current for reducing the number of sensors in order to reduce noise, economic costs and latency. The performance of the proposed control scheme is investigated via simulation and the results confirm the effectiveness of this scheme.

articleTitle: Computational Fluid Dynamics and Experimental Analyzes of a Pico-Hydrokinetic Turbine
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The use of different kind of renewable sources of energy is strongly encouraged globally. The practical realization of a pico-hydrokinetic turbine that can be implemented in small rivers must be preceded by the realization and verification of the experimental models because is important to choose the optimal model. In this paper are presented some of the Computational Fluid Dynamics obtained using the Altair SimLab software, AcuSolve solver, and experimental results of the phenomena that appear during the functioning of the turbine model developed by ICPE-CA.

articleTitle: The Impact of the Applied Teaching Activities in the Training of Technical and Digital Competencies and Abilities
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper presents the results of a study, conducted in January 2021, that aimed to evaluate progress in training and developing skills and abilities in technical education and to identify the constraints that persist in this important sector of education. Eighteen students enrolled in master's studies in the study program Power Quality and Electromagnetic Compatibility in Electrical Systems (CECESE) and Energy Systems (SEI), from the Faculty of Electrical Engineering in Craiova have participated in the study. They answered a questionnaire with open and closed questions. The main objective of this study was to find out the opinion of the graduates of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering from Craiova from the study program Electrical and Computer Engineering and Power Systems Engineering, about the importance and efficiency of some of the studied disciplines and whether these disciplines had a strong impact on acquiring and improving technical skills, necessary in the activity of electrical engineer. The main findings of the study refer to the methodologies and practices for assessing the level of training and skills development, the receptivity of the educational system to the changes that occur in modern education. The main recommendations of the study concern the curriculum development.

articleTitle: Educational Buildings in Romania - Survey of Existing Lighting Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Educational buildings (schools and universities) in Romania were equipped in time with several types of luminaires and now most of them are using fluorescent lamps, simple switches and using the same room position from the building completion. During time, lighting norms changed and since 2003 the European norm EN 12464-1 it is used. There is no study on the existing situation of lighting parameters in educational buildings in Romania and this paper is presenting the results of a survey in several schools in Romania and compares the measured results with recommended values. The paper is the base on a study regarding possible measures for energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Heuristic and Metaheuristic Techniques based Distribution Network Reconfiguration. Case study: IEEE 33 Bus System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper deals with distribution network reconfiguration tackled through two approaches. The 1st one refers to a heuristic method named Sequential Switch Opening (SSO). The 2nd one is based on genetic algorithms (GA). To achieve this goal a software tool has been developed. The well-known IEEE 33 bus system is used as case study. The complete AC power flow computing is used for operating conditions. For reconfiguration purposes the binary coded GA has been used.

articleTitle: An Approach on Power Converters Cooling System Optimization
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper presents an approach for optimizing the cooling system dedicated to a given power converter. The optimization is required to reduce the power consumption of this auxiliary module found within the configuration of power converter.

articleTitle: Improving the partial load operation regimes for cogeneration/trigeneration systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper proposed here continues the efforts undertaken to support renewable energy sources and energy efficiency measures for a decrease in fossil fuel consumption and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emissions. Cogeneration has an important role in the increase of the efficiency of power and heat generation, leading to a decrease of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emissions in the tertiary sector. Buildings rehabilitation that became a norm of the last years and/ or the use of solar energy for heating or for domestic hot water could improve the effect of energy efficiency of the energy sector, with a significant decrease of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emissions. However large scale rehabilitation measures should include the combined heat and power plant and the heat distribution system affected by these measures. In cogeneration or trigeneration systems the fuel savings calculated for each separate measure are in fact smaller due to partial load operation regimes of the power plats. The analysis method presented in this paper focuses on the determination of more efficient operation regimes for the combined and heat power plants after the decrease of the heat demand. The method also allows the determination of an optimum ratio between the heat and electrical energy from renewable energy sources within an extended cogeneration system.

articleTitle: An Optimal Sliping Frequency Control Implementation for Induction Traction Motor on dSPACE 1104 DSP Board
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is the implementation of the control algorithm of an optimal sliping frequency control for induction traction motors using the dSPACE DS1104 prototyping board. The control system is tested on a comprehensive experimental setup, based on a drive motor of 3 kW. The control algorithm was previously validated on the drive system virtual Simulink model, with the same parameters as the experimental drive system, so the control system parameters have already been refined. At the same time, not only the control parameters are taken from the virtual system, but the whole control algorithm. This is because the executable program for the DS1104 prototyping board is obtained by compiling a Simulink model. So the experimental system control algorithm a section of the virtual drive system and consequently the experimental results are completely comparable with the initial virtual results. The complete control model is obtained by adding to the control subsystem the Real Time Interface blocks (necessary to make the link between the software (the Simulink model) and the DS1104 hardware (analog to digital converters, pulse width modulators, etc.). The power system is real time controlled by means of a virtual control panel linked to the control model blocks, parameters or signals.

articleTitle: Automotive PM Surface Alternator, Analyse with Experiments
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The electrical energy in a car, when the combustion engine is running, is made, for the most period of time (peak loads can, also, be taken by the battery), by the claw-poles alternator. The article presents an alternator with permanent magnet surfaces in the rotor, the stator being identical, from a constructive point of view, with the stators from the classic alternators (Lundell). The permanent magnets are rectangular in shape and replace the claw-type poles from the the classic alternators with the coiled rotor. To obtain a variable speed, the alternator with permanent magnets is driven by a belt through a three-phase induction motor powered by a variable frequency driver. Experiments were performed with this alternator at variable speed, without and with buck converter (two types) for voltage stabilization, without and with power resistors (of different values) and with lead-acid battery. The use of alternators with permanent magnets in vehicles is another solution for producing electricity and can be a more reliable solution than the classic one.

articleTitle: Thévenin Equivalent Circuits for Magnetisc Coupling Resonators (Series–Series, Series– Parallel) in Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In this paper the equivalent Thévenin circuits for two connections (series-series (ss), series-parallel (sp)) are obtained, for the magnetic coupling coils (resonators), used in wireless active power transfer. Based on the maximum active power transfer theorem, the optimal load parameters (connected to the terminals of the receiver coil) will be determined so that it receives maximum active power.

articleTitle: Dynamic Inversion based Control of DGMSCMGs. Part 2: Control Architecture Design and Validation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper is mainly based on the design and the software validation of a dynamic inversion and Lyapunov theory based control architecture for the high-precision control of the magnetically suspended double gimbal control moment gyros. The complete dynamics of the DGMSCMG systems has been obtained in Part 1 of this paper series. Using this dynamics, in the present work, a dynamic inversion based control system is proposed to cancel the nonlinearities of the plant, as well as to ensure a stable and linear behavior of DMSCMGs. This new control architecture consists of a translation controller, an orientation controller, a stabilization controller, and a nonlinear observer. The dynamic inversion control technique improves the angular rate precision of the AMB-rotor and of the gyroscopic gimbals.

articleTitle: PV Monitoring System using Industrial Internet of Things Technologies based on Graphical Programming
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Photovoltaic Panel Systems are already a commodity, the widespread use of such systems being no longer a pioneering topic. Monitoring these power generation systems is not a trivial task since the hunger of real-time data is growing continuously. The advent of IoT technologies, the ubiquitous presence of communication technologies, including remote areas, are making these solutions easier to develop, deploy and use. This will constitute the nurturing bed for optimization processes, which would eventually rely on Artificial Intelligence. This paper is describing how to design and deploy such data collecting system, emphasizing on its Software Architecture based on graphical programming technologies. Ready-to-run virtual instruments are facilitating real-time measurements and analysis, process data being securely stored and visualized using cloud technologies.

articleTitle: Remote Learning Model to Introduce Transdisciplinary Topics of Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The aim of the paper is to propose a remote learning model based on an appropriate environment to apply a learning scenario built on `Open Ended laboratory' method. The main objective of the work become `to create a test bench for an inter and trans disciplinary topic around diesel electric traction' and to implement it in a remote learning model. The engineering topic is to analyze, trans- and inter- disciplinary, the harmonic distortion of the armature currents of a synchronous generator during the co-operation with a power system which is simulated the operation of a diesel engine. The numerical environment is calculus in Matlab and the remote environment is Google Classroom platform. The purpose of this analyze is to offer an example for future works projects, developed on open ended laboratories scenarios. For been used even in distance learning, the finality of the paper is the remote learning model of this topic.

articleTitle: On the Water-Energy Relationship in the Case of Water Supply Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Energy and water are the main resources that support human well-being. But energy and water systems have a major contribution to intensifying climate changes and climate instability. That is why it is necessary to find a balance between the demand and supply of water and energy. In this paper an analysis of the energy-water relationship is made. There is shown that the growing demand for water and energy makes the interaction between water and energy systems stronger and stronger. The factors influencing this multidimensional connection, defined as water-energy nexus (WEN), are assessed for the general case of energy and water production systems, and for the particular case of urban water supply systems. In the case of a water pumping station, as the main consumer of electricity in the urban water supply system, the energy intensity of WEN is obtained by using monitoring data for a period of one month. The energy intensity value of 0.632 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> is compared with existing data in the literature and new ways to reduce energy and water losses are highlighted.

articleTitle: Considerations Regarding a Nitinol (Ni-Ti)-operated Micropump
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper presents elements regarding the production and testing of a Nitinol-operated micropump. Nitinol is used to build actuating and control systems due to its properties to change its shape under the action of temperature, the more so as it is used in form of springs developing traction force. Finally, the main performance of the micropump developed is presented. Depending on the current chosen for the power supply of Nitinol springs, the system pumps a certain amount of liquid in a certain time. The higher the current, the higher the speed reaction in pumping the liquid, however, it also takes longer time between pumping cycles to cool the springs, so they can revert their direction of movement. For optimal operation, we have to go on an average current of supply of springs, the amount of liquid is average and the cooling time of the springs will still be average.

articleTitle: Adaptive ACOR for solving the TEAM22 benchmark problem
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The present paper studies the efficiency of a previously proposed aACO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</sub> (adaptive Ant Colony Optimization for Real domains) algorithm for solving the TEAM22 (Testing Electromagnetic Analysis Method) benchmark electromagnetic problem. Several variants of aACO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</sub>, with adaptive selection, adaptive construction and adaptive selection & construction combined, are applied on the TEAM22 benchmark and compared with the original ACO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</sub>. The obtained results are also analyzed in comparison with the best results previously obtained with a PSO (Particle Swarm Optimization) based algorithm for the TEAM22 problem.

articleTitle: SteriLightVent - Hybrid UV Lighting Decontamination Device
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Lighting Engineering Laboratory (LEL) of the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca is the main lighting independent consultant around Transylvania (the north-west region of Romania). LEL has many ongoing technical research or consultancy lighting contracts concluded with o lot of private companies, city councils and national regional authorities. Different lighting retrofit LED systems were tested so far. COVID-19 pandemic started in 2020 generated a lot of research regarding the fight against the virus propagation and the most effective sterilization methods. So far there are o lot of studies about the benefits of using ultraviolet type C (UVC) radiation for the decontamination of surfaces or foul air. Based on the previous studies LEL in collaboration with the Clinical Hospital for Infectious Diseases Cluj-Napoca and supported by some Romanian lighting manufacturers and the Romanian Green Building Association (ROGBC) proposed SteriLightVent. The new concept of hybrid UVC decontamination fixture proposed (in the paper) combines two different UVC sterilization technologies: sterilization of surfaces by direct UVC radiation when there are no people in the closed spaces and sterilization of waste air using filters and UVC sources that can be used even in the presence of individuals. Those two different operation modes give SteriLightVent a high flexibility being used for medical offices, hallways, waiting rooms, beauty salons, etc.

articleTitle: Design, Implementation and Testing of a Locking System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper aims to determine the characteristics of intelligent materials, in this case nitinol, but also to determine its behavior in different situations of the application made and tested. To determine the characteristics and behavior of nitinol, a device was made in the form of an actuator that performs a movement due to the forces that are born in this material, forces that are obtained from the change of temperature. The device is called a locking system that performs compression - decompression, respectively closing - opening movements of the actuator, being controlled by the electric current applied to the ends of the nitinol element and can be used in applications such as cars.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Nonlinear Dynamics of a Cubic Modified Chua’s Circuit System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: By reformulating the cubic modified Chua's circuit system as a set of two second order differential equations, we investigate the nonlinear dynamics of this modified version of Chua's circuit system from the Jacobi stability point of view, using the Kosambi-Cartan-Chern geometric theory. We will obtain the five KCC-invariants which express the intrinsic geometric properties of the system, including the deviation curvature tensor which determine the Jacobi stability of the system near equilibrium points.

articleTitle: Demand Side Management and Integration of a Renewable Sources Powered Station for Electric Vehicle Charging into a Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper describes the demand side management of a renewable sources powered station for electric vehicles charging. The integration of the station into the smart grid is also considered. The architecture of the remote control system of the mentioned station is described. A general analysis of how electricity demand can be managed is given. It is also shown how demand management is applied at the charging station for electric vehicles. A controller based on fuzzy logic was then proposed. In this sensitive process of microgrid integration into a smart grid, what is important from the point of view of a smart grid and what is important from the point of view of the owner of a microgrid is analyzed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the voltage supply unbalance and detection of the short-circuit faults in induction machine through the neighboring magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a new way to use magnetic field analysis for the detection of two electrical dissymmetries which appear in the asynchronous machine. The magnetic field is an interesting variable to exploit for the diagnosis of electrical machines because its measurement is easy, completely noninvasive, and uses inexpensive coil flux sensors. The advantage to use this variable is that it is more sensitive to electrical faults than to current or vibration. In the faulty case or voltage supply unbalance, a magnetic dissymmetry occurs which can be found in the external magnetic field measured near the electrical machine. The sensitive harmonics are extracted from the signals delivered by a pair of flux sensors placed around the machine and the data obtained from several positions are analyzed. The amplitude ratio and the correlation coefficient are the parameters used by the proposed diagnosis method. In practice, the user needs to detect whether there is a fault but also to know its origin. The originality of the proposed method is that can detect and classify the type of fault at the same time. The tests are applied for unbalance voltage and short-circuit faults. Obtained results show that the proposed approach makes it possible to detect and to determine the type of fault and for an easy analysis a graphic interpretation is proposed. Thus, the results presented in this paper pave the way to the better classification of different types of faults that appear in electrical machines and so to ensure safe operation in various technical processes.

articleTitle: Automation Control System for Naval Propulsion Retrofitting
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Nowadays, automation systems for naval propulsion groups with gas turbines use programmable logic controllers for a precise and reliable control. The automation system is designed so as to be able to connect using signal cables to the transducers monitoring the engine's parameters, via adapters, so that the command and regulation functions to be fully automatized. These signals are managed by means of the software program implemented in the PLC, and subsequent data acquisition. One of the important problems is the available resource of the propulsion group, until capital repair is required. The remaining lifetime depends on the operating regimes of the gas turbine engine. This problem is more pronounced in the propulsion groups equipping navy ships, where the dynamic regimes of gas turbine engines are much more demanding, and hence the pre-established operating limits may be exceeded. The automation configuration presented herein ensures the accurate computation and precise control of essential parameters for which the direct measurement is not possible using transducers. These parameters are the exhaust gas temperature, the power developed by the engine and implicitly the torque developed at propeller shaft.

articleTitle: Locomotive Diesel Engine Test Stand with Energy Recovery in the Electrical Network
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper presents a test stand for internal combustion Diesel engines, for testing and break-in of locomotive Diesel engines, used in railway traction, with energy recovery in the electrical network. Its realization was carried out by modernizing the test stand of Diesel engines for locomotives from Remarul "16 Februarie" in Cluj-Napoca, resulting an experimental model presented in this paper. The stand is designed for verification and monitoring tests of technical parameters (electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic) for the correct operation of the locomotive Diesel engine. The novelty of the stand presented in this paper, consists in the automation of the entire testing process of the Diesel engines for the realization of the mentioned stand as well as the energy recovery in the electrical network. The stand includes modern equipment and components, data display and storage equipment for the main measured parameters as well as software dedicated to the application.

articleTitle: Integrated System for Monitoring Aircraft Structural Condition by Using the Strain Gauge Marks Method
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This study emphasizes the importance of aircraft structural condition monitoring and, furthermore, on the analysis of the aging process of military aircraft structural constitutive materials, during flight. Nowadays, aircraft are predominantly built from composite materials with at least two layers with different mechanical properties, which combined, result in a new composite material with highly superior resilience and elastic properties. This paper has its focus on improving the process of monitoring the structural condition of highly maneuverable military jet aircraft by using the strain gauge marks methods. As a result of the continuous research and testing, it has been proved that the operational resource of the aircraft structure, provided by the manufacturer, can be easily reached in a lot lesser flight hours than initially anticipated, by engaging the aircraft in specific operational missions and, therefore, inflicting pronounced fatigue on the aircraft structure.

articleTitle: Optimal location and sizing of multiple PV systems in a distribution network using Marine Predators Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Optimal location and sizing of renewable energy sources (RES) represents an important instrument in the efficient operation and planning of the electric networks. Solar energy is the second most used RES after wind and it contributed as an important factor, in the last two decades, to improving the European energy supply security. The main purpose of this paper is to present a mathematical model for optimal location and sizing of multiple photovoltaic (PV) systems in a distribution network using Marine Predators Algorithm (MPA). The objective function consists in minimizing the active power losses, while maintaining all bus voltages and line currents within the acceptable range. Multiple scenarios are considered in order to integrate the daily and seasonal variations of both PV output and load demand. Finally, the solution with the lowest active power losses for a one-year period is selected. The results provided by the MPA are compared, in terms of performance with those supplied by a genetic algorithm (GA).

articleTitle: Aspects Regarding of Electrical Isolation of Spark Plugs Used at Spark-Ignition Engines
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper analyses the isolation resistance, the dielectric absorption ratio and the polarization index of some common spark plugs used for spark ignition engines. The experimental analysis is performed on new, middle-life spark plugs and some at the end of their life, by measuring the isolation resistance with megohmmeters, at various test voltages. The quality of electrical insulation may also differ for new spark plugs. For a batch of used spark plugs and at the end of their life, an analysis of the isolation resistance, the dielectric absorption ratio and the polarization index was performed before and after two cleaning methods: mechanical and chemical. It was found that mechanical cleaning better improves the electrical performance of spark plugs compared to the chemical method. However, some of the spark plugs have irreversibly affected the quality of the electrical insulation, and the cleaning methods do not improve the electrical performance of the spark plugs.

articleTitle: Possibilities to Improve Energy and Economic Efficiency for an Overhead Transformer Station and Related Network
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In the distribution networks 20/0.4 kV, which generally have a large extent, in terms of the number of transformation, switching, measuring and protection equipment and considerable lengths, there is the problem of energy and economic efficiency of both substations and related networks on the one hand, but also the increase in the quality of the electricity supply service on the other hand.The paper analyzes a PTA and the related 0.4 kV network, which have a long history and a high degree of technological consumption. For this, the PTA was monitored in order to determine the energy losses and the voltage drops. The acquired data allowed the calculation of these losses and voltage drops on all sections of the network.In order to improve the energy and economic parameters and to secure the network, certain technical measures considered appropriate in such situations were analyzed. The proposed measures could be technically and economically feasible.

articleTitle: Overvoltage Produced by Lightning Impulse in High Power Transformers - Parameters that Influence their Transmission
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The overvoltages caused by the lightning impulse, at the level of the high power transformer, have a great importance from the design stage. For these reasons, this paper presents the electrical parameters that influence the transmission of overvoltages in the transformer windings, but also a method for determining them. To simulate the phenomenon caused by lightning impulse on the transformer, an application was realized in the LabVIEW development environment. This application allows to determine the values of the transmitted overvoltages between the transformer windings. The study was performed on a transformer of 54/73 MVA, TTUS-ONAN, 110/15 / 6.6 kV, and the results obtained were validated by laboratory tests.

articleTitle: Dynamic Inversion based Control of DGMSCMGs. Part 1: Obtaining the Nonlinear Dynamic Model
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper series presents a complete dynamic model associated to a magnetically suspended double gimbal control moment gyro by considering the rotor-gimbal interactions, as well as the design and software validation of a dynamic inversion and Lyapunov theory based controller for DGMSCMG high-precision control. We start with the obtaining of the nonlinear dynamics of the gyroscopic system, the aims of the controller being: 1) to ensure both the robustness and the high accuracy convergence of the system; 2) to handle the interferences between channels. Part 1 of this paper series provides the necessary theoretical developments associated to the complete dynamics of the DGMSCMGs, while Part 2 contains the design and software validation of the dynamic inversion based control architecture.
